b4af2d450e96756d585f52feea7c93dcf168a8cf.summary: This page is a repository file listing, not a threat report. It shows the title of a YARA rule file for a Windows trojan called WarmCookie, archived in 2026, followed by a long index of rule file names across Linux, macOS, multi-platform and Windows categories. The index covers malware families, ransomware, rootkits, hacking tools, wipers and vulnerable drivers. The text describes no specific incident, actor, date or technique, so no facts are recorded.

b4b3125d2c2217c262572cfe6023dc08d49c7c4e.summary: Morphisec describes the FIN7 cybercrime group, which it says primarily targets US businesses to steal payment card data. The report covers how FIN7's attack chain changed over the four months to an attack on October 8 to 10, 2017, and how those changes helped evade security solutions. It also covers a June 2017 fileless campaign against US restaurants. The report says FIN7 is closely tied to the Carbanak Gang, but that evidence so far falls short of directly equating the two.

b418f8a762ec974f7ad7a7d02f01d69e0f3db0dc.summary: ESET Research white paper on OpenSSH backdoors found in the wild. Analysts grouped their samples into 21 families, 12 of them undocumented at the time. Common features include hardcoded backdoor passwords, credential stealing, anti-logging and root-access tampering. Stolen credentials go to local files, network channels, DNS or email. The paper links the Kamino backdoor to DarkLeech and Carbanak, and reports a custom honeypot where operators of two backdoors were observed. The infection vector is hard to determine.
